newsitem.title: USA: Freeport Copper signs pact for Busang stake.
newsitem.headline: Freeport Copper signs pact for Busang stake.

text.p: Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc. said Thursday it has signed a binding agreement to acquire a 15 percent stake in two Indonesian companies to be formed that are expected to benefit from the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia.

The deal, which was announced last week, was signed with Bre-X Minerals Ltd., Freeport partner in the venture. This puts to rest any market speculation that Freeport would back out of its deal with Bre-X at the last minute, analysts said.
The new companies are expected to be granted contracts to explore and develop mining rights in the Busang II and Busang III areas of Indonesia.
The companies will be owned 45 percent by Bre-X, 40 percent by Indonesian interests, including the government of Indonesia, and 15 percent by Freeport-McMoran.
Under the deal, Freeport-McMoran is to be the sole operator of the Busang II and Busang III properties.

In consideration for the transaction, Freeport-McMoran has agreed to provide 25 percent of the total estimated cost of delineating a proven reserve and constructing the initial Busang mine complex, up to $400 million.

In addition, it has agreed to arrange, on behalf of the Indonesian companies, a $1.2 billion project financing commitment from Chase Manhattan Corp. for the remaining estimated costs of the initial Busang mine complex.

The company said it has undertaken a due diligence review of the Busang gold properties and expects to prepare a feasibility study during the second quarter that will form the basis for the initial mine and mill development.
